title: 3D spinning dropped items with rarity glow and light
player_outcome: Loot on the ground is the real 3D item, slowly spinning and bobbing: swords, coins, dirt cubes. Rare items glow in their rarity colour. Fallen Stars, torches and souls light up the ground around them.
design: Verified: DroppedItemRenderer draws Y-billboard icon quads with glow = rarity > 0 ? 0.08 : 0 (DroppedItemRenderer.cs:50-56); nothing emits light.
Split DroppedItemRenderer.cs into lifecycle and a new DroppedItemRenderer.Visuals.cs.
Items with a GLB use a pooled MeshInstance3D with the cached PropLibrary mesh, scaled so the max AABB extent is 0.45 m. Blocks use BlockItemMeshes cubes (P3-06). The billboard stays as a fallback.
Spin at 1.5 rad/s about Y, always bobbing. NoGravity items (P3-29) float and pulse.
Rarity glow: an additive billboard halo from a pool with a shared material and instance colour = rarity colour × pulse, for rarity ≥ 1 or Glows (expert −12 cycles hue).
Lights: DroppedItemRenderer.Lights provider for DynamicLights (items with HeldLight or Glows), so the count is limited by the preset.
Async model loads via ResourceLoader.LoadThreadedRequest; the billboard shows until ready; ≤ 1 new model instantiation per frame.
voxel_light updated round-robin (¼ of drops per frame).
tests: Smoke basic.cmds: 'drop copper_broadsword 1 0 0 2' / 'drop gold_coin 5 1 0 2' / 'wait 1' / 'assert props.problems == 0' / 'assert errors == 0'
verification: Lavapipe screenshots of mixed drops by day and a glowing fallen star at night
perf: 150 drops → gd.drops < 0.5 ms; no frame spike when a new item type drops (perf report max)
risks: Async loading must not race QueueFree of pooled visuals.
The hover name label is P2 (crosshair names).
